lessons.title: The Off-Chain Half of a dApp

slots.practicalActivity: Sketch a one-page architecture diagram of a dApp showing the on-chain contract plus the five off-chain jobs this course covers (RPC access, event listening, indexing, oracle reads, wallet-session auth), labeling where each piece actually runs.
slots.deliverable: A saved architecture notes file (`dapp-architecture.md`) mapping each off-chain job to the chapter that teaches it.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a free Infura or Alchemy account, generate an API key, and call the resulting RPC endpoint directly with curl's `eth_blockNumber` JSON-RPC method to confirm you're talking to a live synced node.
slots.deliverable: Terminal output (saved to a text file) showing the current Ethereum block number returned by your own RPC key.

slots.practicalActivity: In a new Node.js project, install ethers.js (or viem), point it at your RPC endpoint from the previous lesson, and write a script that fetches the ETH balance and the latest block number for a known public address.
slots.deliverable: A working `read-chain.js` script that prints a real balance and block number to the console.

slots.practicalActivity: Get a funded test wallet on a public testnet (e.g. Sepolia) from a faucet, then extend your script to sign and send a small ETH transfer programmatically with ethers.js/viem, printing the resulting transaction hash.
slots.deliverable: A `send-tx.js` script plus the real testnet transaction hash it produced, viewable on a block explorer.

slots.practicalActivity: Modify `send-tx.js` to call `estimateGas` before sending, log the estimate versus the actual gas used from the receipt, and manually track/increment the nonce across two back-to-back sends from the same wallet.
slots.deliverable: Console output comparing estimated vs. actual gas for two transactions sent with manually-managed nonces.

slots.practicalActivity: Configure two different RPC endpoints (e.g. your Infura key and a public Chainlist endpoint) and write a wrapper function that catches a rate-limit/error response from the first and automatically retries against the second.
slots.deliverable: A `provider-failover.ts` module with a working fallback path, demonstrated by forcing the primary call to fail.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: combine the reading, sending, and gas/nonce lessons into one reusable `ChainClient` module — read balances/blocks, send a signed transaction, and handle nonce + gas estimation internally — then use it to send two transactions back to back without a nonce collision.
slots.deliverable: A `chain-client.ts` module demonstrated by sending two sequential testnet transactions with a passing manual test.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: harden your `ChainClient` with the provider-failover wrapper so every read/write call tries a backup RPC provider automatically; verify it by temporarily pointing the primary provider at an invalid URL.
slots.deliverable: An updated `chain-client.ts` that successfully completes a read and a send even with its primary RPC URL broken.

slots.practicalActivity: Pick a well-known deployed ERC-20 contract on a testnet (e.g. a faucet token) and identify its `Transfer` event signature and indexed parameters from its ABI/Etherscan page.
slots.deliverable: A short notes file listing the event name, its indexed parameters, and the contract address you'll use for this chapter's labs.

slots.practicalActivity: Write two small scripts against the same contract: one polling `getLogs` on an interval, one using a WebSocket provider's `on('Transfer', ...)` subscription, and compare how quickly each notices a transfer you trigger yourself.
slots.deliverable: Two scripts (`poll-events.js`, `ws-events.js`) plus a one-line note on which one caught your test transfer faster.

slots.practicalActivity: Add confirmation-depth logic to your polling script so it only treats an event as 'final' once it's N blocks deep, and reason through what would happen to an unconfirmed event if the chain reorged it out.
slots.deliverable: An updated `poll-events.js` that only emits an event after a configurable confirmation depth.

lessons.title: Building a Simple Event Listener Service

slots.practicalActivity: Combine polling, confirmation depth, and an in-memory log of seen events into one standalone Node service that prints every confirmed Transfer for your test contract as it happens.
slots.deliverable: A runnable `event-listener-service.js` demonstrated live against real testnet transfers you trigger.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: make your event-listener service restart-safe by persisting the last processed block number to a local file (or SQLite), so a restart resumes from where it left off instead of re-scanning from genesis or missing events.
slots.deliverable: An updated event listener that, when killed and restarted mid-run, resumes from its saved last-block checkpoint.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: trigger five test transfers in quick succession on your test contract, run your listener service against them, and produce a log proving zero duplicate and zero missed events.
slots.deliverable: A `listener-run.log` file showing exactly five captured Transfer events matching five real testnet transactions.

lessons.title: Why You Can't Just Query the Chain

slots.practicalActivity: Try to answer a realistic product question ('show this user their last 50 token transfers') using only direct RPC calls (`eth_getLogs` over a large block range) and note exactly where it breaks down (rate limits, block-range limits, time).
slots.deliverable: A short writeup of the RPC-only approach's failure points that motivates indexing.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a free account on The Graph's Subgraph Studio and browse 2-3 existing public subgraphs for well-known protocols to see what entities and queries they expose.
slots.deliverable: Notes on one existing subgraph's schema/entities that you'll model your own subgraph after.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a `schema.graphql` defining a `Transfer` entity (from, to, value, timestamp, txHash) for your test ERC-20 contract.
slots.deliverable: A working `schema.graphql` file for the subgraph you'll deploy in this chapter's lab.

slots.practicalActivity: Write the AssemblyScript mapping handler that takes the raw `Transfer` event and writes a new entity matching your schema from the previous lesson.
slots.deliverable: A `mapping.ts` handler file that compiles against your schema.

slots.practicalActivity: Deploy your subgraph to Subgraph Studio against your test contract, wait for it to sync, and run a GraphQL query for the transfers you generated earlier in this course.
slots.deliverable: A log of a real GraphQL query result returning your test contract's actual Transfer entities.

slots.practicalActivity: List the operational tradeoffs (cost, latency, control) between the subgraph you just deployed and a managed indexing API (e.g. Alchemy's Transfers API), using your own deployment as the concrete comparison point.
slots.deliverable: A short comparison table: your subgraph vs. a managed indexer, for this specific use case.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: extend your subgraph's schema and mapping to also track a running `totalTransferred` counter per address, redeploy, and confirm the aggregate updates correctly across multiple test transfers.
slots.deliverable: A redeployed subgraph whose GraphQL query returns a correct running total for at least one test address.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: write a backend script that queries your deployed subgraph's GraphQL endpoint (instead of raw RPC calls) to answer the original 'show this user's last 50 transfers' question, and compare the code's simplicity to the raw-RPC attempt.
slots.deliverable: A `query-subgraph.js` script returning real transfer history pulled from your subgraph.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a one-paragraph explanation of why a smart contract can't call an external HTTP API directly to get an ETH/USD price, using the 'oracle problem' terminology from the lesson.
slots.deliverable: A short written explanation saved alongside your other course notes.

slots.practicalActivity: Using ethers.js/viem, connect to a real public Chainlink ETH/USD price feed contract on a testnet and call `latestRoundData()` to read the current price on-chain.
slots.deliverable: A script printing a real, current ETH/USD price pulled directly from a Chainlink feed contract.

slots.practicalActivity: Read through Chainlink Automation's docs for a sample upkeep contract and identify what `checkUpkeep`/`performUpkeep` would need to contain for a 'rebalance when price crosses X' use case.
slots.deliverable: Short notes outlining the checkUpkeep/performUpkeep logic you'd need for a price-triggered action.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a Node script that polls the Chainlink feed from the previous lesson every N seconds and logs an alert the moment ETH/USD crosses a threshold you set.
slots.deliverable: A running `price-trigger.js` that logs a real alert when the live feed crosses your chosen threshold.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: wire your price-trigger script to also call a stub backend endpoint (a console.log or local Express route) simulating 'notify the user' the moment the Chainlink price crosses the threshold, tying this chapter together into one working off-chain price-triggered pipeline.
slots.deliverable: An end-to-end demo: live Chainlink price read, threshold check, and triggered 'notification' call, logged from a single run.

slots.practicalActivity: Read the EIP-4361 (SIWE) message format spec and hand-write one valid SIWE message for a test domain and wallet address.
slots.deliverable: A text file containing one correctly-formatted SIWE message.

slots.practicalActivity: In a small Node/Express app, build an endpoint that takes a SIWE message + signature, recovers the signing address with ethers.js/viem, and checks it matches the claimed wallet.
slots.deliverable: A working `/verify` endpoint that correctly accepts a real signed message from your own test wallet and rejects a tampered one.

slots.practicalActivity: Extend the `/verify` endpoint to issue a signed JWT (or server-side session cookie) on successful signature verification, and add a protected `/me` route that requires it.
slots.deliverable: A working login flow: sign a SIWE message, get a session token, call `/me` successfully with it, and fail without it.

slots.practicalActivity: Read through a relayer/meta-transaction pattern (e.g. OpenZeppelin's or Biconomy's docs) and diagram how a user's signed intent gets relayed and paid for by someone else's gas.
slots.deliverable: A short diagram/notes file explaining the relayer pattern in your own words.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: combine the SIWE, verification, and session lessons into one working backend auth flow — a test script that signs a SIWE message with a test wallet, posts it to your server, receives a session token, and uses it to call a protected route.
slots.deliverable: A passing end-to-end test script exercising the full SIWE login flow against your own Express server.

slots.practicalActivity: Review: walk back through all five chapters' code (RPC client, event listener, subgraph, oracle trigger, SIWE auth) and write a short README tying them together as the five off-chain services a real dApp backend needs.
slots.deliverable: A `README.md` summarizing the five working components you built in this course and how they'd plug into a real dApp.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can stand up a Node/TypeScript backend service that reads and writes to a live blockchain via RPC providers, listens for and indexes on-chain events through a deployed subgraph, pulls live oracle price data to trigger off-chain actions, and verifies wallet-signed logins end to end — the full off-chain half of a working dApp.
